title: Felix and the Current
premise: Casper Galloway, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries after a disaster he refuses to explain, is hired by his old rival Mara Voss to lead a crew up the Serrin River to its forbidden source, where a dying mining magnate believes a glacial spring can restore him. The expedition is illegal, the season is closing, and Casper discovers the client's daughter, Wren, is the child of the man who died in the accident that ruined him. As the river narrows and loyalties fracture, Casper must choose between protecting his crew, confessing the truth of his past, and stopping Wren from repeating his mistake. At the source, the miracle proves to be poison in beautiful packaging; Casper sacrifices his last chance at redemption to bring Wren home alive, and the two broken guides walk out together into an uncertain but honest future.
about_author: Jonah Underhill is a former river surveyor who spent a decade mapping waterways across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes from a cabin above a cold tributary, where he still measures life in miles.

chapters.title: The Blacklist
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Fifteen years after being banned from two countries' guiding registries, Casper runs marginal trips on the Serrin's lower reaches. A letter arrives bearing Mara Voss's seal — the rival whose testimony ended his career. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in pride, the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: An Offer Measured in Miles
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Mara offers triple pay to guide her crew upstream to the Serrin's forbidden source for a wealthy client. Casper refuses until he learns the client is Aldous Crane — father of the man who died under Casper's rope. Emotional beat: guilt weaponized into obligation.

chapters.title: The Crew Assembles
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Crane joins the expedition as her father's eyes, meeting the ragged team: geologist Okafor, cook-brothers Penn and Rill, and the legend himself, Casper Galloway. She expects a coward; she finds someone watching her like a ghost. Emotional beat: wary curiosity curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Signs at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The first week goes smoothly until Okafor finds old survey markers — Casper's own, fifteen years stale, far beyond any legal route. Someone on the crew photographs them and sends word downstream. Emotional beat: unease that the mountain remembers more than its people do.

chapters.title: Mara's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flashback-tinged chapter: Mara recalls the disaster on the North Col and why she testified against Casper — and what she has never told anyone about that night. Now she needs his knowledge of the upper gorge. Emotional beat: ambition braided with buried shame.

chapters.title: The First Portage
chapters.summary: Penn's POV. The crew hauls boats over a rockslide as weather turns. Casper saves Rill from a collapsing chute with reflexes no honest guide should have. Wren begins asking questions Casper won't answer. Emotional beat: grudging respect hardening into obsession with the truth.

chapters.title: What the River Forgets
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Campfire confessions loosen the crew; Casper tells half-truths about his blacklisting. Wren reveals she's dying too — a slow illness her father's fortune cannot cure, which is why he seeks the source. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's wounds.

chapters.title: The Turncoat
chapters.summary: Rill's POV. It emerges one crew member has been reporting their position to a conservation authority that will arrest them at the border of the protected headwaters. Paranoia splits camp. Mara quietly identifies the informant — and pays them off instead. Emotional beat: trust as currency, devaluing fast.

chapters.title: Gorge of the Sworn-Off
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. They enter the canyon Casper swore never to revisit, site of the original tragedy's aftermath. He leads them through by memory alone, and Wren realizes he's been here since — many times, alone. Emotional beat: grief made navigable only by repetition.

chapters.title: Crane's Voice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A satellite call from Aldous Crane: the syndicate funding the trip wants samples first, cure second, and if the source can't be owned it will be dammed. Wren realizes she was sent to legitimize a land grab. Emotional beat: love against duty, the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. A storm strands the crew on an exposed shelf; supplies are lost when a cache tumbles into the river. Rill breaks his wrist. Casper makes the call to push on rather than retreat — the same call that killed a man fifteen years ago. Emotional beat: history threatening to rhyme.

chapters.title: The Confession at High Camp
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Cornered by Wren, Casper finally tells the truth: her brother died testing a route Casper had already condemned, because Aldous Crane pressured the expedition to summit on schedule. Casper took the blame; Mara let him. Emotional beat: catharsis that changes nothing yet everything.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Wren turns on Mara, not Casper. Mara admits she stayed silent to win the guiding contract of a lifetime. The crew splinters: some side with Wren, some with the payday. Emotional beat: power's corruption laid bare around a thin fire.

chapters.title: The Dam Surveyors
chapters.summary: Penn's POV. The crew stumbles on an advance team staking the headwaters for Crane's syndicate — the trip was always cover. Mara, confronted, chooses at last: she burns the syndicate's radio and commits to the crew. Emotional beat: redemption arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Upstream of Maps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Past all markers, the river becomes something older — braided, violent, unnamed. Wren's illness worsens at altitude; Casper carries her stretches without complaint. Emotional beat: tenderness growing in ground that shouldn't hold anything.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. They reach the glacial spring: luminous, mineral-rich, and toxic — Okafor tests it and finds heavy metals that mimic vitality before they kill. The 'miracle' would have murdered Aldous slowly and beautifully. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Aldous Arrives
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A helicopter lands with Aldous Crane and syndicate men, summoned by the informant's final message. Aldous drinks from the spring despite warnings, needing to believe. Emotional beat: a father choosing a beautiful lie over his living daughter.

chapters.title: The Standoff at the Headwaters
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Syndicate men move to seize the site and silence witnesses. Casper triggers a controlled icefall to block the helicopter pad — using the exact skill that once killed, now to save. Emotional beat: climax; identity reclaimed through choice, not denial.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The retreat downriver through worsening weather, Aldous deteriorating from the water he drank, Wren refusing to leave him. Casper carries both father and daughter's weight literally and otherwise. Emotional beat: duty transformed — no longer obedience, but care.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. At the ranger station below the protected zone, the crew gives joint testimony exposing the syndicate. Casper surrenders to the blacklist willingly, asking only amnesty for the crew. Emotional beat: justice accepted on its own terms.

chapters.title: Amnesty
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Months later: the headwaters granted protection, Aldous recovering but diminished, Wren's illness in remission after treatment she almost refused. She petitions successfully to have Casper's record reviewed. Emotional beat: grace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Measured in Years
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Spring on the lower Serrin: Casper, reinstated, leads Wren and Mara on an open, legal run downriver. He stops measuring in miles. Emotional beat: resolution — love chosen over duty's ghost, identity rebuilt from truth.
